Author: @Destructor8031
Content:
It's amazing that it's got into this point, the internet is one of the greatest tools ever invented. It gives us the ability to access any information anywhere about practically anything. Get somehow we've let it get to the point where the majority of the internet is basically controlled by three different companies and if those companies have an issue we lose most of the internet.

 It's not just a fault of these three companies and I'm not going to give them shit for having this issue because everybody makes mistakes and nothing is perfect. But we're the ones who have collectively decided to depend on these three services. If one website or platform dies you can go to another one but you can't if all of those platforms depend on the same thing that has an outage. 

This is why we need decentralized internet and more people need to start hosting their own stuff. If what you need to host is basic and it's not actually that difficult or that impractical to do it yourself, I'm not saying we shouldn't have centralized services as they have their place but their place shouldn't be controlling access to the majority of the internet.

Author: @Tnu1138
Content:
This is what happens when infrastructure becomes centralized: it's astonishing that the majority of internet uptime relies on just five companies. Almost any global system is inherently fragile. Remember when a ship got stuck in a canal, halting and delaying shipping for weeks? This incident underscores the need for our games and software to prioritize offline functionality. Features that require an online connection should be supplementary, not the core reason we use a program.

I find it frustrating that so many services now demand 24/7 internet connectivity. Years ago, you could still enjoy a movie or play a game even if your internet was down. Today, if your internet goes out or if Google experiences issues, you can't access anything. What amazes me is that in 2025, humanity still hasn't grasped the simple, historical lesson of what happens when you put all your eggs in one basket.

How can anyone still be shocked by this at this point?
